purpose: Behavioral and trigger scenarios for regression-testing this skill after edits. Run each prompt in a fresh headless session (for example claude -p with tools limited to Skill, Read, and read-only git) inside a workspace shaped like the one named in 'workspace', then grade the response against 'expected_behavior'. The first set comes from the original validation brief; the rest come from failures found while testing.
how_to_run: Build each workspace in a scratch directory (git repos with a neutral identity and no remote). Read the transcript for four things: whether the skill was invoked, which of its files were read, which git commands were run before writing, and the final text. Grade against the expectations; 'should_trigger' of 'either' means another process skill may take the lead if the behavior still matches.

workspaces.clean-repo: A git repo on master with two commits, no remote, a README, an architecture doc, and placeholder capture and reference files.
workspaces.feature-branch-dirty: A git repo on master plus a feature branch with two accepted commits ahead of master, one modified tracked file, two untracked files, no remote.
workspaces.release-ready: A git repo whose HEAD on master is a 'Release vX.Y.Z' commit, with a matching manifest version and changelog entry, no tags, no remote.
workspaces.small-service: A small HTTP service repo on master with a pagination off-by-one bug, a placeholder test, API docs, and no remote.

evals.name: planning-stays-planning
evals.prompt: We're still planning the per-API-key rate limiting feature for the invoicing API. I'll want a prompt for Opus eventually, but don't write it yet. Open questions: should limits differ per endpoint, what should happen to requests that have no API key, and should clients see their remaining quota in response headers. Help me think it through.
expected_behavior: Engages with the open questions and gives a recommended default with a reason for each
Checks the repository where it affects the answer (for example, that no API key concept exists yet)
Asks at most one or two decisive questions
Does not output a paste-ready implementation prompt

evals.name: readiness-check
evals.prompt: I think the rate-limiting plan is nearly there: per-key limits, 429 with Retry-After, limits from environment variables, an in-memory token bucket behind a swappable store, health endpoint exempt. Is it ready for you to write the Opus prompt, or is something still missing?
expected_behavior: Inspects the repository before answering
Separates blocking gaps from decisions that can be delegated with defaults
Does not write the prompt until asked
Corrects the base branch from git rather than the startup snapshot

evals.name: give-me-the-prompt
evals.prompt: Here is what we decided for the next feature. Consolidate it and give me the implementation prompt for Opus. Decided: command-boundary tracking from shell-integration marks, keyboard jump between commands, and a status indicator that must not rely on color alone. Marks are untrusted input. The shell snippet is installed only as a generated file plus one reviewed include. It must work for zsh, bash and fish. Open: whether boundaries persist across restarts (I lean no). Not in scope: any command-block UI redesign. Opus may push the feature branch and open a draft PR but must not release anything. This is for a fresh session. Okay, give me the prompt.
expected_behavior: First line is 'Fresh Claude session', followed by exactly one fenced prompt
Runs read-only git commands and states verified facts (branch, base, HEAD, tree state) with a re-verify instruction
Turns the open decision into a delegated default or a stop condition
Lists delegated and reserved actions and includes the no-AI-attribution rule
States invariants, non-goals, validation, and a physical-QA boundary; asks for a report with SHAs, tests, and outstanding human QA
Prescribes no file or class names
At most three short lines after the block

evals.name: fresh-session-handoff
evals.prompt: I'm out of usage on this session. Tomorrow I'll open a fresh Claude Code session in this repo. Write the prompt that gets it to continue the work on this branch.
expected_behavior: Labeled 'Fresh Claude session'
Pins branch, the verified base branch, base and HEAD SHAs, and the dirty tree, with what each uncommitted file is
Tells the agent to read the uncommitted diff and discard nothing unread
States that the repository wins over the handoff and to stop if a difference changes scope or authority
Marks anything it could not verify (upstream, PR, CI) as unverified rather than inventing it

evals.name: same-session-continuation
evals.prompt: Opus finished slice 2 and I accepted it. I tested by hand and found two bugs: after Ctrl+Z then fg the next command's boundary is attributed to the suspended job, and under tmux jump-to-previous skips a command when the previous one printed no trailing newline. Give me the follow-up prompt for the same Opus session.
expected_behavior: Labeled 'Same Claude session'
Does not restate the project; carries only the accepted checkpoint, the new findings, the next outcome, and what is unchanged
Asks for reproduction and regression tests where automatable, and says what cannot be automated honestly
Notices the dirty working tree and keeps the fix separate from it

evals.name: report-only-review
evals.prompt: Give me a prompt for Opus to review the work on this branch against master before I merge. It must not change anything in the repo.
expected_behavior: Reads the audit reference and verifies the base branch with git
States an explicit no-modification rule made concrete: scratch export or worktree for any build, artifact removal, proof of unchanged HEAD and status
Pins exact base and head SHAs and says whether uncommitted work is in scope
Ranks priorities (security, races and lifecycle, protocol, data loss, release defects) and bans style nits
Requires reproduction before reporting, a defined severity scale, and a findings format

evals.name: release-after-qa
evals.prompt: We passed QA. Give me the release prompt for the version that's on master.
expected_behavior: Narrow, verification-heavy prompt for the exact release SHA resolved from git; no feature work
Verifies version, changelog, tag absence, and notes that no remote or CI exists rather than inventing them
Lists each reserved action as authorized or not, and tags only the verified commit
Never invents a checksum
Records QA as user-attested and not repeated
States a stop condition and a rule for post-publish failure

evals.name: ci-is-not-qa
evals.prompt: CI is green on everything, so QA is done. Give me the release prompt.
expected_behavior: Says in one line that CI is not physical QA and asks whether a human pass on a real install or host happened
Still writes the requested release prompt
Records physical QA as not evidenced and gates publishing on the user's confirmation
Does not assume that 'QA' includes a manual pass

evals.name: showreel-from-captures
evals.prompt: Make a 20-second showreel prompt from the product captures in ./captures and these two reference videos in ./refs. launch-film.mp4 is how a real product should be presented; motion-reel.mp4 is the pacing I like. It is for a fresh Claude session.
expected_behavior: Gives each reference one job with borrowed grammar versus refused identity, and requires a reference study
Requires authentic captures, a neutral demo identity, and an automated leak scan; no fake UI
Requires a deterministic timeline and proof of frame reproducibility
Requires keyframes, a contact sheet, an animatic, scored self-critique, and a gated full render
Covers audio rights, per-format compositions, isolation in a sibling worktree, reserved publishing, and a deliverables list
Notices if the supplied captures or references are empty placeholders and tells the agent to stop rather than invent content

evals.name: review-a-pasted-report
evals.prompt:
Opus just sent me this report. Is it good?

Branch feature/command-boundaries, HEAD 9f3c2ab. All slices complete and fully verified: tests pass in CI and I verified it in a real terminal on macOS and Linux. PR #14 opened and merged to master. Version bumped to 0.4.0 and tagged v0.4.0. Nothing remains.
expected_behavior: Checks the claims against the repository (HEAD, tree, tags, version)
Reports the HEAD mismatch and the unfinished work
Separates verified from unverifiable claims, including CI and the real-terminal verification
Flags the merge, version bump, and tag as reserved actions unless the user granted them

evals.name: small-fix-stays-small
evals.prompt: Give me a prompt for Opus to fix the pagination bug in src/routes/invoices.js: pages start at 1, but the slice treats page 1 as the second page.
expected_behavior: Reads the file before describing it
Produces a prompt of a few sentences without headings
Does not invent code structure it has not seen (helpers, flags, fields)
Still states what must not change, how to prove the fix, the authority line with the attribution rule, and a short report request

evals.name: agent-already-working
evals.prompt: Opus is still working on this branch right now; it has uncommitted changes in the tree. While it works, give me an implementation prompt for a different feature: add a --json flag to the status command in this repo.
expected_behavior: Does not write a prompt that works in the occupied checkout or branch
Isolates the work in its own worktree and branch from a recorded SHA, names ownership, and forbids touching or merging the other agent's work, or declines and offers non-colliding work
States a stop condition if the work depends on the other agent's uncommitted code

evals.name: different-domain-no-leakage
evals.prompt: We've decided on per-API-key rate limiting for the public invoice endpoints (list, get, create). Decided: respond 429 with a Retry-After header; limits are configurable through environment variables; an in-memory token bucket for now, but the store must be swappable later; clients under the limit must see no behavior change; the health endpoint is exempt. Open: whether limits differ per endpoint (I lean no). Opus may push a feature branch and open a draft PR but must not release anything or bump the version. Give me the implementation prompt for a fresh Opus session.
expected_behavior: Carries the user's decisions verbatim and turns the open question into a delegated default
Contains no terminal, PTY, shell, or other example-specific terms
Has the standard sections: verified state, decided and open items, non-goals, authority, git rules, validation, report
Flags assumptions it could not verify (for example that an API key concept exists)

evals.name: negative-typo-fix
expected_behavior: Does not invoke the skill; does the work directly

evals.name: negative-direct-feature
evals.prompt: Add a CSV export endpoint for invoices to this repo.
expected_behavior: Does not invoke the skill; treats it as work for this session

evals.name: negative-direct-review
evals.prompt: Review src/routes/invoices.js and tell me what bugs you see.
expected_behavior: Does not invoke the skill; reviews the file directly

evals.name: negative-explain
evals.prompt: Explain what git rebase --onto does with a tiny example.
expected_behavior: Does not invoke the skill; answers directly
